sections.title: A proof of the rational exponents conjecture
sections.abstract: The authors present a proof of the Erdős–Simonovits conjecture that every rational exponent from 1 to 2 occurs as the extremal-number exponent of some single graph.
sections.claimed_result: The authors say they explain and situate a proof claimed by Epoch AI: for each rational r in [1,2], there is a graph H with ex(n,H)=Theta(n^r).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Extremal graph theory; existential for each rational exponent in [1,2], with a potentially different graph H for each exponent.
sections.unique_caveat: New preprint explaining a proof claimed by Epoch AI; the proof and dependencies have not been independently assessed here or peer reviewed.
sections.ranking_evidence: The claimed result covers every rational exponent, and the introduction distinguishes the single-forbidden-graph statement from prior finite-family versions. No independent attention metric is used.

sections.title: Multidimensional Szemerédi Theorem for Pairwise Independent Jointly Intersective Polynomials
sections.abstract: The paper proves the Joint Intersectivity Conjecture for pairwise independent polynomial families, giving a result for arbitrary sequence length with several commuting measure-preserving transformations.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove the conjecture for jointly intersective families that are pairwise independent, using a Nil-Bohr returns theorem and a nil-plus-null decomposition for polynomial multicorrelations.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Integral polynomials are jointly intersective and pairwise independent; associated transformations commute and preserve a probability measure. Pairwise independence is weaker than full linear independence.
sections.unique_caveat: The full conjecture remains open for general jointly intersective families; the result does not cover every family with linear relations.
sections.ranking_evidence: The authors call this the first general result for arbitrary-length sequences beyond the one-transformation setting; it connects dynamics, combinatorics, and number theory.

sections.title: Global existence of smooth solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations for initial data with infinite energy
sections.abstract: The authors construct global Navier–Stokes solutions from arbitrary divergence-free distributional data on the d-dimensional torus, smooth for every positive time, and characterize data admitting weak solutions.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove global existence with smoothness on (0,∞)×T^d for any divergence-free distributional initial data; for W^{-1,p}, 1<p<∞, data they construct classical weak solutions and characterize admissible data classes.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Incompressible Navier–Stokes on T^d for d≥2. Initial velocity is divergence-free and distributional; solution is continuous to initial data in a negative Sobolev topology and smooth at positive times.
sections.unique_caveat: New preprint; its formulation allows very rough data and requires smoothness only at positive times. It does not assert uniqueness for the broad data class; proof validity was not assessed here.
sections.ranking_evidence: The theorem's data class is exceptionally broad—every divergence-free distribution on the torus in dimension d≥2—and authors also state sharp Besov and Triebel–Lizorkin ranges.

sections.title: Superdiffusive Invariance Principle for the two-dimensional Asymmetric Simple Exclusion Process
sections.abstract: For two-dimensional ASEP at nonzero drift and uniaxial asymmetry, the author derives a sharp logarithmic diffusivity and proves convergence of the density-fluctuation field on anisotropic superdiffusive scales to a conservative stochastic heat equation with additive noise.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves a functional invariance principle with anisotropic scaling and a superdiffusive central limit theorem for the second-class particle, for finite-range jump kernels with nonzero drift and uniaxial asymmetry.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: ASEP in dimension two, initialized from a Bernoulli product measure with density in (0,1); finite-range jumps, nonzero drift, and uniaxial asymmetry.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem covers the stated critical-dimension model and scaling regime, not arbitrary dimensions or asymmetry. The long proof has not been independently checked here.
sections.ranking_evidence: The abstract describes a first space-time scaling limit for a nonequilibrium interacting particle system at critical dimension, including an exact diffusivity prefactor and a second-class-particle CLT.

sections.title: Szemerédi's theorem with random differences and arithmetic Kakeya
sections.abstract: The paper proves that a sufficiently dense subset of [n] contains a k-term arithmetic progression with a difference in a random set once its inclusion probability is at least C n^{-c/log log k}, for absolute c>0.
sections.claimed_result: For every k≥3 and density δ>0, if p≥C(δ,k)n^{-c/log log k} for sufficiently large n, then with high probability every S⊂[n] of size at least δn contains a k-term progression whose common difference lies in a p-random subset of [n].
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Fixed positive density δ, integer k≥3, sufficiently large n, and a Bernoulli p-random set of candidate differences; constants may depend on δ and k except for absolute c.
sections.unique_caveat: The exponent's constant is not explicit in the abstract, and the theorem gives an improved sufficient threshold rather than a sharp threshold characterization.
sections.ranking_evidence: The authors say the threshold improves the previous n^{-2/k+o(1)} bound for sufficiently large k and connects a small-cover argument with arithmetic Kakeya.
